risks.risk: 仓库迭代极快（7 天内 10+ commit），你的 PR 可能迅速冲突
risks.mitigation: 保持每个 PR 小而专注（单文件/单模块），rebase 频率提高；优先做测试/文档类 PR，这类冲突概率低于 src 改动

risks.risk: 无 GPU 导致无法验证 CUDA 路径的真实数值正确性
risks.mitigation: 把验证拆成两层：CPU 数值回归（本地）+ Colab T4 最终确认（阶段 90 前申请免费 T4 做几十分钟验证）；在 PR 描述显式标注 'verified on CPU, CUDA pending'

risks.risk: 核心维护者关注点可能不在 scheduler/scripts，你的方向被边缘化
risks.mitigation: 用证据绑定：scheduler 是 README 三核心之一、scripts 是新增模型入口、benchmarks CPU 基线直接支持官方 Apple Silicon 立场；在 PR 描述引用 PHILOSOPHY 与 README 原文

risks.risk: tests/schedulers/ 现有测试可能已隐含 GPU 假设，CPU 运行会暴露环境差异
risks.mitigation: 先跑全量现有测试建立 baseline，再决定是加 skipIf(not cuda) 还是统一改用 CPU 小模型；与 sayakpaul 在 Issue 中对齐测试策略

risks.risk: scripts/ 96 个脚本质量参差不齐，smoke test 可能触发隐藏 bug 被误认为你的 PR 引入
risks.mitigation: smoke test 只验证 import + 映射函数输出键一致性，不验证数值；发现已有 bug 单独开 Issue，不阻塞你的 PR

risks.risk: MacBook Air 16GB 内存受限，部分测试可能 OOM
risks.mitigation: 在 tests/conftest.py 加 device fixture 自动降级到 CPU + 小 batch；benchmark 默认用 64x64 或更小分辨率

risks.risk: Hugging Face 仓库权限申请流程不透明，triage 权限可能延迟
risks.mitigation: 先从 Issue 回复、Discord 帮助、PR review 贡献可见度；权限是结果而非前提

issues.title: gfx1201 (RDNA4) SageAttention attention backend: aiter package or Hub kernel?
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

On AMD Radeon RDNA4 GPUs (gfx1201: Radeon AI PRO R9700 / R9600D, RX 9070 series), diffusers has no quantized attention backend:

- `SAGE` and `SAGE_HUB` are CUDA builds.
- The ROCm Hub FlashAttention kernel (`kernels-community/aiter-flash-attn`) ships tuning configs for gfx942 / gfx950 / gfx1250 only.

So these GPUs use native SDPA.

aiter has a SageAttention kernel for gfx1201: `aiter.gfx1201_sage_attention(q, k, v, softmax_scale)`, ROCm/aiter#6390 (under review).

- INT8 QK^T and FP8 PV with FP32 accumulation; Q/K are quantized per 32-row block and V per channel inside the kernel.
- Inputs: BF16 `[B, S, H, 128]`, Q/K/V of equal shape, no mask, non-causal.

MiniMax-H3 in diffusers matches that contract exactly. `MiniMaxH3AttnProcessor` passes no mask, the attention is self-attention with head dim 128, and the input is BF16. The same applies to the token refiner.

For reference, the same kernel as an opt-in vLLM-Omni backend (vllm-project/vllm-omni#8792, draft) on MiniMax-H3 T2VA: 2 x R9700 TP2, 1344x768, 4 s, 8 steps.

| Backend | Denoise per step | Request latency | Video PSNR vs SDPA |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| SDPA | 20.9 s | 186 s | reference |
| gfx1201 SageAttention | 11.3 s | 109 s | 33.9 dB |

**Describe the solution you'd like.**

An opt-in diffusers attention backend for gfx1201 SageAttention. It would never be selected by default, and it would reject unsupported inputs (masks, causal, head dim other than 128, unequal Q/K/V shapes) with a clear error.

It would support Ulysses context parallelism (inference only, no LSE needed), so MiniMax-H3 can run with its existing `_cp_plan` on 2+ GPUs.

Before writing it, I'd like to check which delivery you prefer, given that #14436 moved ROCm FlashAttention from the `aiter` pip package to a Hub kernel:

1. **`AITER_SAGE`, using the `aiter` package.** The backend imports `aiter` and calls the op. It is a small diffusers change, but it adds back an optional `aiter` dependency and needs an aiter release that contains ROCm/aiter#6390.
2. **`AITER_SAGE_HUB`, a Hub kernel.** We publish the kernel as a `kernels` package. Like `kernels-community/aiter-flash-attn`, it would be a universal `torch-rocm` build: precompiled gfx1201 code objects plus a small Python loader registered as a torch custom op. diffusers would only add a `_HubKernelConfig` entry and the backend function. This does not depend on an aiter release. The open question is which Hub repo it should live in.
3. **A ROCm variant of `kernels-community/sage-attention`**, so the existing `SAGE_HUB` works unchanged. Its `sageattn` would route gfx1201 inputs it supports to this kernel and the rest to SDPA.

**Describe alternatives you've considered.**

- Keep SDPA on gfx1201. That leaves about 1.8x on MiniMax-H3 attention unused.
- A custom attention processor in user code. It works, but every model needs its own processor, and it does not compose with `set_attention_backend` or context parallelism.

**Additional context.**

I can implement whichever option you prefer, with tests and a MiniMax-H3 end-to-end comparison against SDPA on 2 x R9700 using Ulysses CP. A sparse variant (Sol-Attn, ROCm/aiter#6292) also exists. Following the note in `attention_dispatch.py` about per-model-tuned sparse methods, I am not proposing it here.

cc @sayakpaul

AI assistance: this proposal was drafted with the help of an AI coding assistant (GitHub Copilot). The numbers above were me

issues.title: [Z-Image] joint_attention_kwargs={"scale": ...} is silently ignored when loading LoRA weights
issues.body: ### Describe the bug When a LoRA is loaded into a Z-Image pipeline, `joint_attention_kwargs={"scale": ...}` has no effect. The argument is accepted, documented and stored in `self._joint_attention_kwargs`, but it is never forwarded to `self.transformer(...)` ([pipeline_z_image.py#L533](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/blob/85c9fa4caee33d1c5b473395784471d2d7957c1b/src/diffusers/pipelines/z_image/pipeline_z_image.py#L533)). `ZImageTransformer2DModel.forward` ([transformer_z_image.py#L894](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/blob/85c9fa4caee33d1c5b473395784471d2d7957c1b/src/diffusers/models/transformers/transformer_z_image.py#L894)) has neither a `joint_attention_kwargs` argument nor the `@apply_lora_scale("joint_attention_kwargs")` decorator. No error or warning is raised: the LoRA is silently applied at full strength whatever scale is requested. Other pipelines such as Flux handle this correctly: `FluxTransformer2DModel.forward` is decorated with `@apply_lora_scale("joint_attention_kwargs")` and `FluxPipeline` passes `joint_attention_kwargs=self.joint_attention_kwargs` to the transformer. LoRA loading itself works, and `pipe.set_adapters(name, weight)` does change the strength, because it sets the weights directly on the LoRA layers. What is missing is the per-call `scale`. All six Z-Image pipelines have the same pattern: `ZImagePipeline`, `ZImageControlNetPipeline`, `ZImageControlNetInpaintPipeline`, `ZImageImg2ImgPipeline`, `ZImageInpaintPipeline` and `ZImageOmniPipeline`. ### Reproduction ```python import numpy as np import torch from diffusers import ZImagePipeline pipe = ZImagePipeline.from_pretrained("Tongyi-MAI/Z-Image-Turbo", dtype=torch.bfloat16) pipe.enable_model_cpu_offload() pipe.load_lora_weights("artificialguybr/PIXELART-REDMOND-ZIMAGETURBO") def generate(**kwargs): return pipe( "Pixel Art, PixArFK, a red fox sitting in the snow", height=1024, width=1024, num_inference_steps=8, guidance_scale=0.0, generator=torch.Generator("cpu").manual_seed(0), **kwargs, ).images[0] with_lora = generate() # LoRA at full strength scale_zero = generate(joint_attention_kwargs={"scale": 0.0}) # expected: the LoRA has no effect pipe.disable_lora() without_lora = generate() # reference: no LoRA at all def same(a, b): return np.array_equal(np.asarray(a), np.asarray(b)) print("scale=0.0 identical to LoRA at full strength:", same(scale_zero, with_lora)) print("scale=0.0 identical to no LoRA:", same(scale_zero, without_lora)) ``` Output on current `main`: ``` scale=0.0 identical to LoRA at full strength: True scale=0.0 identical to no LoRA: False ``` Expected: `False` / `True`, since `scale=0.0` should cancel the LoRA's contribution. Actual: `True` / `False`, so the scale is ignored. The image below comes from a longer comparison script. The model, LoRA, prompt and seed are the same in every tile; only the scaling method changes. From left to right: no LoRA, LoRA at full strength, `joint_attention_kwargs` scale 0.0, `joint_attention_kwargs` scale 0.5, `set_adapters` weight 0.0, `set_adapters` weight 0.5. - Both `joint_attention_kwargs` tiles are pixel-identical to full strength (mean absolute difference 0.0). - `set_adapters(0.0)` is identical to no LoRA. - `set_adapters(0.5)` differs from full strength by 0.194 (LoRA vs no LoRA: 0.263).

issues.title: VaeImageProcessor.denormalize() raises AttributeError for NumPy inputs
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

`VaeImageProcessor.denormalize()` is documented to accept both NumPy arrays (`np.ndarray`) and PyTorch tensors (`torch.Tensor`). However, passing a NumPy array raises an `AttributeError` because the implementation uses the PyTorch-specific `.clamp()` method.

**Root cause**

In `src/diffusers/image_processor.py`, line 234:

```python
return (images * 0.5 + 0.5).clamp(0, 1)
```

NumPy arrays do not implement `.clamp()`, despite being included in the function's type annotations and documentation.

**Expected behavior**

The function should denormalize NumPy inputs to `[0, 1]`, preserving the input type and existing PyTorch behavior.

**Proposed direction**

Use input-type-appropriate clipping, such as `np.clip()` for NumPy and `.clamp()` for PyTorch, or clarify the supported types if NumPy support is not intended.

I'd be happy to contribute a fix after discussing the preferred approach with maintainers.

### Reproduction

```python
import numpy as np
import torch
from diffusers.image_processor import VaeImageProcessor

values = [-2.0, -1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 2.0]

numpy_input = np.array(values, dtype=np.float32)
torch_input = torch.tensor(values, dtype=torch.float32)

# PyTorch succeeds
print("PyTorch:", VaeImageProcessor.denormalize(torch_input))

# NumPy raises AttributeError

issues.title: [modular] `SequentialPipelineBlocks` gets `required` wrong in both `inputs` and `required_inputs`
issues.body:
## What happens

A `SequentialPipelineBlocks` has two views of its inputs, and each gets the `required` flag wrong in a different way.

**1. `required_inputs` keeps names that an earlier sub-block produces.** In `Flux2CoreDenoiseStep`, `prepare_latents` declares `latents` as optional and produces it, and `set_timesteps` does the same for `timesteps` and `num_inference_steps`. The denoise loop then requires all three. `inputs` says optional, `required_inputs` says required:

```python
from diffusers.modular_pipelines.flux2.modular_blocks_flux2 import Flux2CoreDenoiseStep

core = Flux2CoreDenoiseStep()
print([(i.name, i.required) for i in core.inputs if i.name in ("latents", "timesteps", "num_inference_steps")])
print(sorted(core.required_inputs))
```

```
[('latents', False), ('num_inference_steps', False), ('timesteps', False)]
['batch_size', 'guidance', 'latent_ids', 'latents', 'num_inference_steps', 'prompt_embeds', 'timesteps', 'txt_ids']
```

Nothing produced those values from the user's point of view either way, but the first view is the right one here: the block fills them in itself.

**2. `inputs` keeps the first declaration's flag even when a later sub-block requires the value and nobody produces it.** In `StableDiffusion3I2ICoreDenoiseStep`, `additional_inputs` declares `image_latents` as optional, `prepare_img2img_latents` requires it, and no sub-block produces it. The user has to pass it, so it is required. `inputs` says optional, `required_inputs` says required:

```python
from diffusers.modular_pipelines.stable_diffusion_3.modular_blocks_stable_diffusion_3 import StableDiffusion3I2ICoreDenoiseStep

core = StableDiffusion3I2ICoreDenoiseStep()
print([(i.name, i.required) for i in core.inputs if i.name == "image_latents"])
print("image_latents" in core.required_inputs)
```

```
[('image_latents', False)]
True
```

Here the second view is the right one.

`LoopSequentialPipelineBlocks` has the same two problems.

## Why

`inputs` walks the sub-blocks in order, skips a name once an earlier sub-block produced it, and otherwise keeps the first declaration as is. It never looks at what later sub-blocks require.

`required_inputs` is computed separately, as a plain union of every sub-block's `required_inputs`. It never looks at what earlier sub-blocks produce.

## Effect

The docstrings are rendered from `inputs`, so they are wrong in case 2 directly. In case 1 the wrong flag reaches the docstring through blocks that rebuild `required` from their sub-blocks' `required_inputs`, which is why the `*optional*` marker is missing from `latents`, `timesteps` and `num_inference_steps` in the Flux2 auto blocks and in Anima, Cosmos, Helios, Hunyuan Video 1.5, LTX, LTX-2, MiniMax H3, QwenImage, SD3, SDXL, Wan and Z-Image. Anything that reads `required_inputs` directly, such as the Mellon node config, gets case 1 wrong too.

## Fix

Decide `required` in the single ordered walk: a name is required if some sub-block requires it, no earlier sub-block produced it, and no earlier declaration gives it a default. Derive `required_inputs` from that, so there is only one answer. PR to follow.

---

issues.title: Enable KV cache offloading for a better speed-memory trade-off
issues.body:
We have KV Caching in a bunch of models now, including Flux2 and QwenImage 2.1.

While it helps make inference faster, it also increases memory consumption. For example, in QwenImage 2.1, with KV Caching, peak memory goes from 32.3G -> 36.0G. 

To make this trade-off better for our users, I think we could start thinking about KV cache offloading.

The offloading could have different flavors:

* Offload to and onload from RAM (sync, will compromise speed)
* Offload to and onload from RAM but async (like group offload, should provide the best trade-off)
* Same options but with secondary storage

Need to think about a nice abstraction for this. @asomoza do you think this could be helpful? @DN6 let me know your thoughts too.

issues.title: PNDMScheduler.set_timesteps crashes with NumPy broadcasting error for fewer than 4 inference steps
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

`PNDMScheduler.set_timesteps()` raises an internal NumPy broadcasting error when `num_inference_steps` is `1`, `2`, or `3` with the default `skip_prk_steps=False`.

The error occurs during construction of the PRK timesteps. The scheduler uses `self.pndm_order = 4`, but for fewer than four inference steps, the following expression produces arrays with incompatible shapes:

```python
prk_timesteps = np.array(self._timesteps[-self.pndm_order :]).repeat(2) + np.tile(
    np.array([0, self.config.num_train_timesteps // num_inference_steps // 2]),
    self.pndm_order,
)
```

For `num_inference_steps=3`, the left-hand array has shape `(6,)`, whereas the right-hand array has shape `(8,)`, resulting in a `ValueError`.

**Observed behavior:**

- `num_inference_steps=1`: broadcasting error, shapes `(2,)` and `(8,)`
- `num_inference_steps=2`: broadcasting error, shapes `(4,)` and `(8,)`
- `num_inference_steps=3`: broadcasting error, shapes `(6,)` and `(8,)`
- `num_inference_steps=4`: succeeds

This behavior is reproducible with all three timestep-spacing modes (`leading`, `linspace`, and `trailing`). The same low-step configurations succeed when `skip_prk_steps=True`.

**Expected behavior:** If PRK requires at least four inference steps, `set_timesteps()` should raise a descriptive validation error rather than exposing an internal NumPy broadcasting error. If fewer steps are intended to be supported, the PRK timestep construction should handle those cases correctly.

A possible validation is:

```python
if not self.config.skip_prk_steps and num_inference_steps < self.pndm_order:
    raise ValueError(
        f"`num_inference_steps` must be >= {self.pndm_order} when "
        f"`skip_prk_steps=False`, got {num_inference_steps}."
    )
```

I searched existing Diffusers issues and PRs for this specific failure and did not find an exact duplicate.

### Reproduction

**Minimal reproduction:**

```python
from diffusers import PNDMScheduler

scheduler = PNDMScheduler()
scheduler.set_timesteps(3)
```

**Reproduction across inference-step counts:**

```python
from diffusers import PNDMScheduler

for n in [1, 2, 3, 4]:
    try:
        scheduler = PNDMScheduler()
        scheduler.set_timesteps(n)
        print(f"n={n}: OK")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"n={n}: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
```

Output:

```text
n=1: ValueError: operands could not be broadcast together with shapes (2,) (8,)
n=2: ValueError: operands could not be broadcast together with shapes (4,) (8,)
n=3: ValueError: operands could not be broadcast together with shapes (6,) (8,)
n=4: OK
```

**Control case (PRK disabled):**

```python
from diffusers import PNDMScheduler

for n in [1, 2, 3]:
    scheduler = PNDMScheduler(skip_prk_steps=True)
    scheduler.set_timesteps(n)
    print(n, scheduler.timesteps.tolist())
```

The control case succeeds for all three values.

**Existing test coverage:**

```bash
python -m pytest tests/schedulers/test_scheduler_pndm.py -q
```

Result:

```text
32 passed, 1 skipped
```

The existing PNDM scheduler tests pass, but do not appear to cover the low-step PRK failure.

### Logs

```shell
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<string>", line 1, in <module>
  File "E:\diffusers\src\diffusers\schedulers\scheduling_pndm.py", line 217, in set_timesteps
    prk_timesteps = np.array(self._timesteps[-self.pndm_order :]).repeat(2) + np.tile(

issues.title: load_video() leaks temporary files when remote video decoding fails
issues.body:
﻿### Describe the bug

`diffusers.utils.load_video()` creates a temporary file using `NamedTemporaryFile(delete=False)` when downloading a video from a URL. However, the temporary file is removed only after video decoding completes successfully.

If decoding raises an exception (for example, when attempting to load a corrupted GIF), execution never reaches the cleanup statement, leaving the downloaded file on disk.

Repeated failures may accumulate unnecessary temporary files.

### Steps to reproduce

The following reproduction uses a mocked HTTP response and requires no GPU or external network access.

```python
import os
import tempfile
from unittest.mock import patch

from PIL import UnidentifiedImageError
from diffusers.utils import load_video


class FakeResponse:
    status_code = 200

    def iter_content(self, chunk_size=8192):
        yield b"THIS_IS_NOT_A_VALID_GIF"


with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp_dir:
    with (
        patch(
            "diffusers.utils.loading_utils.requests.get",
            return_value=FakeResponse(),
        ),
        patch(
            "diffusers.utils.loading_utils.tempfile.tempdir",
            tmp_dir,
        ),
    ):
        try:
            load_video("https://example.com/corrupt.gif")
        except UnidentifiedImageError as e:
            print(type(e).__name__, str(e))

        print("Remaining files:", os.listdir(tmp_dir))
```

### Actual behavior

The decoder raises `UnidentifiedImageError`, but the temporary file remains on disk.

Observed output:

```text
Exception: UnidentifiedImageError

Remaining temporary files:
tmpeiv6c3cc.gif | Size: 23 bytes

BUG REPRODUCED: Temporary file was not deleted!
```

### Expected behavior

Temporary files created for remote video downloads should be deleted even when downloading or decoding fails. The original exception should continue to propagate.

### Root cause

In `src/diffusers/utils/loading_utils.py`:

- Line 97 creates a temporary file with `delete=False`.
- The subsequent code downloads and decodes the video.
- Line 142 removes the temporary file only after successful decoding.

Any exception before the cleanup statement bypasses file deletion.

### Proposed fix

Ensure exception-safe cleanup of downloaded temporary files using `try/finally`, covering both download and decoding failures.

Add regression tests verifying that temporary files are removed on both successful and failed operations.

### Environment

- Repository: huggingface/diffusers
- Source revision reproduced: 899c9f3fd
- OS: Windows
- Device: CPU
- Reproduction: mocked HTTP response with corrupted GIF content
- No pretrained models required
- 
### Who can help?

@sayakpaul @yiyixuxu

I would appreciate your review and any suggestions regarding exception-safe temporary-file cleanup and regression test coverage in `load_video()`.

issues.title: Explore llama.cpp/ggml quantization kernels for our GGUF integration
issues.body:
Transformers recently landed support for running llama.cpp / ggml quantization schemes directly, backed by a set of ggml kernels distributed through the `kernels` library. Write-up: https://huggingface.co/blog/transformers-llama-cpp-quants

This looks potentially interesting for our GGUF integration in Diffusers:

- Today our GGUF support dequantizes on the fly; the ggml kernels could let us run quantized ops natively instead, which should help both memory and speed.
- It could also open up nicer MPS / local-inference angles, which is a frequent ask for Diffusers users.

Relevant kernels (currently being moved from `transformers-community` to the [`ggml-org`](https://huggingface.co/ggml-org) org):

- https://huggingface.co/kernels/transformers-community/ggml-quantization
- https://huggingface.co/kernels/transformers-community/ggml-gated-delta-net
- https://huggingface.co/kernels/transformers-community/ggml-norm
- https://huggingface.co/kernels/transformers-community/ggml-attn

Next steps to figure out:

1. Which of these kernels are actually applicable to diffusion model architectures (quantization/norm most likely; attn depends on our attention dispatch).
2. Whether they can be plugged into the existing `GGUFQuantizer` path via the `kernels` library.
3. Benchmark quality/speed/memory vs. the current dequantize-on-load behaviour, including on MPS.

---

issues.title: Per-module alphas of kohya text encoder LoRAs collapse to the most common alpha (alpha_pattern keys stop at the parent module)
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

When a kohya-format SDXL/SD1.5 LoRA has different `.alpha` values across text encoder modules, every text encoder module ends up with the most common alpha. The minority modules get the wrong scale.

`get_peft_kwargs` builds the text encoder `alpha_pattern` with `".".join(k.split(".down.")[0].split(".")[:-1])` ([peft_utils.py#L189](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/blob/main/src/diffusers/utils/peft_utils.py#L189)). For a network alpha key such as `text_model.encoder.layers.1.self_attn.to_k_lora.down.weight.alpha`, that yields `text_model.encoder.layers.1.self_attn`, which is the parent attention block and not the `k_proj` module. PEFT's `get_pattern_key` matches pattern keys against the end of the module name, so the key matches no LoRA module and the default `lora_alpha` (the most common value) applies everywhere.

The UNet branch keeps the module name, so the UNet is not affected. The same result occurs with a text encoder that still has the `text_model` level (e.g. `CLIPTextModelWithProjection`), so this is independent of #14872.

For scale: in a library of ~8.9k SDXL kohya LoRAs, 59 have per-module text encoder alphas (values from 0.5 to 6 at the same rank, mostly character LoRAs), so their text encoder modules can be off by up to 12x.

### Reproduction

```python
import torch
from diffusers import StableDiffusionXLPipeline
from transformers import CLIPTextConfig, CLIPTextModel

config = CLIPTextConfig(
    hidden_size=8, intermediate_size=16, num_hidden_layers=2, num_attention_heads=2,
    vocab_size=50, max_position_embeddings=8, bos_token_id=0, eos_token_id=1, pad_token_id=1,
)
text_encoder = CLIPTextModel(config)

rank = 4

def kohya_module(name, alpha):
    return {
        f"lora_te1_text_model_{name}.lora_down.weight": torch.ones(rank, 8),
        f"lora_te1_text_model_{name}.lora_up.weight": torch.ones(8, rank),
        f"lora_te1_text_model_{name}.alpha": torch.tensor(alpha),
    }

# Two modules with alpha 1.0 (the most common value) and one with alpha 4.0.
lora = {
    **kohya_module("encoder_layers_0_self_attn_q_proj", 1.0),
    **kohya_module("encoder_layers_0_self_attn_out_proj", 1.0),
    **kohya_module("encoder_layers_1_self_attn_k_proj", 4.0),
}

state_dict, network_alphas = StableDiffusionXLPipeline.lora_state_dict(lora)
StableDiffusionXLPipeline.load_lora_into_text_encoder(
    state_dict, network_alphas, text_encoder=text_encoder, prefix="text_encoder", adapter_name="test"
)

k_proj = text_encoder.encoder.layers[1].self_attn.k_proj
print("k_proj scaling:", k_proj.scaling["test"], "expected:", 4.0 / rank)
print("peft alpha_pattern:", text_encoder.peft_config["test"].alpha_pattern)
```

### Logs

```shell
k_proj scaling: 0.25 expected: 1.0
peft alpha_pattern: {'text_model.encoder.layers.1.self_attn': 4.0}
```

### System Info

- 🤗 Diffusers version: 0.41.0
- Platform: Linux (WSL2) x86_64
- Python version: 3.14.3
- PyTorch version (GPU?): 2.13.0+cu130 (True)
- Huggingface_hub version: 1.33.0
- Transformers version: 5.16.1
- Accelerate version: 1.15.0
- PEFT version: 0.20.0
- Safetensors version: 0.8.0
- Using GPU in script?: No
- Using distributed or parallel set-up in script?: No

### Who can help?

@sayakpaul @BenjaminBossan

issues.title: WanCausalConv3d copies every activation with F.pad. Let the conv do the spatial padding.
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

`WanCausalConv3d.forward` zero-pads height, width and time with `F.pad`, then runs an unpadded `nn.Conv3d`. `F.pad` writes a full copy of the activation on every call, and the Wan VAE calls this for every conv on every latent frame.

**Describe the solution you'd like.**

Only the time axis needs manual padding, because it is causal and the amount depends on the cached frames. Height and width are plain symmetric zero padding, so the conv can do them itself:

```python
self.temporal_padding = 2 * self.padding[0]
self.padding = (0, self.padding[1], self.padding[2])
```

`forward` then pads only the time axis, and skips `F.pad` when the cache already supplies the temporal context. The result is the same, since the module uses zero padding.

On an A10G with torch 2.11.0+cu128, `AutoencoderKLWan.decode` for 33 frames at 512x512 gets about 6% faster:

| dtype | mode | `main` | with the change |
|---|---|---|---|
| float32 | eager | 5150 ms | 4838 ms |
| float32 | `torch.compile` | 4888 ms | 4579 ms |
| float16 | eager | 3048 ms | 2873 ms |
| float16 | `torch.compile` | 2727 ms | 2553 ms |
| bfloat16 | eager | 3046 ms | 2872 ms |
| bfloat16 | `torch.compile` | 2726 ms | 2552 ms |

Peak memory is unchanged. Decoding the latents of a real 33-frame 512x512 video, the output is bit-identical to `main` on CPU (float32 and float64) and on GPU with cuDNN disabled. With cuDNN, 0.3% of 8-bit values change by one level (max difference 1.6e-3 on a [-1, 1] scale, 94.9 dB PSNR), because cuDNN picks its algorithm from the call's arguments.

I would cover two classes in one PR:

- `WanCausalConv3d` in `autoencoder_kl_wan.py`
- `QwenImageCausalConv3d` in `autoencoder_kl_qwenimage.py`, which is a hand copy of it

**Describe alternatives you've considered.**

`QwenImage21CausalConv3d` has the 2D version of the same pattern (`F.pad` over height and width, then an unpadded `nn.Conv2d`). I have not measured it, so I would leave it out unless you want it in the same PR.

**Additional context.**

The change replaces the private `_padding` attribute with `temporal_padding`. Nothing else in `src/` reads `_padding`, and state-dict keys do not change.

I have the fix ready on a branch, with a test that checks the new conv against the original pad-then-conv math for each kernel configuration, with and without cached frames. I used an AI agent to help prepare it, so per the contributing guide I am opening this issue first. I can open the PR as soon as a maintainer is happy with the approach.

issues.title: LTX-2.5 SDR-To-HDR IC-LoRA: how should it be structured?
issues.body:
**What**
[`Lightricks/LTX-2.5-22b-IC-LoRA-SDR-To-HDR`](https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.5-22b-IC-LoRA-SDR-To-HDR) can't run in diffusers today. `LTX2HDRPipeline` targets the LTX-2.3 LogC3 LoRA. The LTX-2.5 one (Lightricks' `ltx_pipelines.hdr_ic_lora.HDRICLoraPipeline`) needs:

1. ACEScct input/output transforms;
2. a video-only, single-stage distilled path conditioned on the LoRA's precomputed scene embedding (no text encoder, no CFG);
3. seam keyframes: 1-frame SDR guides plus generated slots at each 24/32-frame seam, decoded by a keyframe-aware diffusion decoder (`decoder.type_emb`, joint attention with the nearest keyframe planes).

I opened #14966, #14974 and #14975 for this before discussing it here, sorry about that. I'm closing them and would like to agree on the shape first.

**What I measured** (H200, real weights, `hiker.mp4` from `documentation-images`, against the reference at LTX-2 `9ec55f9f`)
- (1)+(2): final latent 50.0 dB, output 38.4 dB; inputs, RoPE positions, masks and token order identical.
- (3): final latent 52.4 dB, token-level checks at 70 dB or better.

**Checkpoint blocker**
The `diffusion_decoder` in `Lightricks/LTX-2.5-Diffusers` doesn't match the current original VAE (`ltx-2.5-video-vae`): it has no `decoder.type_emb`, and none of its decoder tensors match. Decoder-only parity against the reference is 44.4 dB (plain) / 35.2 dB (keyframes) with the published weights, and 62.2 / 68.6 dB once re-converted from the original file. Reported in https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.5-Diffusers/discussions/19. Keyframe decoding can't ship against the current Hub weights.

**Questions**
1. A mode of `LTX2HDRPipeline` (`hdr_transform="acescct"`, which changes the inputs, components, schedule and decoder), a separate `LTX2SDRToHDRPipeline`, or modular blocks?
2. Does diffusers want the HLG BT.2020 10-bit MP4 / EXR writers (optional OpenEXR dependency), or should export stay on the user side?
3. Keyframe decoding touches the same decoder code as #14694. Should it wait for #14694 and be built on its scheduler-owned loop, as a model-only PR after the Hub decoder is re-converted?

My suggested order, if that works for you: (a) ACEScct transforms + SDR-To-HDR without seams, in whatever shape you prefer; (b) the keyframe-aware decoder, after #14694 and the checkpoint fix; (c) seam keyframes in the pipeline; export separately or not at all.

issues.title: LTX-2: decouple the RoPE time base from the playback frame rate (Slow-Motion-Control LoRA)
issues.body:
**What**
[`Lightricks/LTX-2.5-22b-LoRA-Slow-Motion-Control`](https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.5-22b-LoRA-Slow-Motion-Control) expects the diffusion stage to be conditioned on `fps / speed` while the video keeps its real frame rate. Lightricks' `distilled_speed_demo.py` does exactly that. Without it, the LoRA gives no speed control.

**Why `frame_rate` alone doesn't cover it**
In the LTX-2 pipelines and modular blocks, `frame_rate` also sizes the generated audio (`num_frames / frame_rate`) and converts the duration head's seconds into frames. Setting it to `fps / speed` therefore shortens the audio and inflates the predicted frame count. On the tiny test pipeline, `frame_rate=120` gives 9 audio tokens instead of 43, and 121 frames instead of 25 when `num_frames` is omitted.

**Proposal**
An optional `conditioning_frame_rate` (default: `frame_rate`) used only for the positional time axis: video, keyframe and reference coords, plus the transformer `fps`. Audio sizing, the duration head and the output keep following `frame_rate`. This is the split the DFR pipelines already make internally with `conditioning_fps`.

Implementation proposed in #14967. Does this scope (classic pipelines + modular blocks) look right to you?

issues.title: `ModelMixin.from_pretrained` on a sharded checkpoint fails under `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1` even when fully cached (`_get_checkpoint_shard_files` still calls `model_info`)
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

**What happens.** With `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1` set and the checkpoint fully cached, `SomeModel.from_pretrained("<repo id>")` raises `huggingface_hub.errors.OfflineModeIsEnabled` whenever the checkpoint is sharded (it has a `*.safetensors.index.json`). Single-file checkpoints load fine in the same setup. Passing `local_files_only=True` as well works around it. The env var alone is the documented way to run offline, and it is the only option when the call happens inside a library you do not control.

**Why.** `_get_checkpoint_shard_files` checks that the shards exist on the Hub before calling `snapshot_download`, and it skips that check only when `local_files_only` is truthy:

```python
# src/diffusers/utils/hub_utils.py, main @ da1d382, lines 433-435
# If the repo doesn't have the required shards, error out early even before downloading anything.
if not local_files_only:
    model_files_info = model_info(pretrained_model_name_or_path, revision=revision, token=token)
```

`ModelMixin.from_pretrained` passes the caller's `local_files_only` straight through (`modeling_utils.py` line 1297), and that is `None` when the user relies on `HF_HUB_OFFLINE`. So `model_info` runs, and `huggingface_hub` refuses the request because offline mode is on. Earlier steps in the same load already handle offline mode: revision resolution logs `Could not reach the Hub ... Using cached commit hash`, and the config and index come from the cache. Only this pre-check makes the load fail. The guard comes from #12005, which fixed the `local_files_only=True` case (#11948). The env-var case was reported in #11447, which was closed citing #11428, a pipeline PR that does not touch this function.

With `huggingface_hub` 1.33, `snapshot_download` called afterwards also uses the network when it gets an already-resolved revision and the cache has no `trees/<commit>.json` listing. That listing is missing from caches written by older `huggingface_hub` versions and from hand-copied caches. So the fix should also pass the offline state to `snapshot_download`, as shown below.

I can open a PR for this once a maintainer confirms the approach.

### Reproduction

Loads a real sharded checkpoint, first online to fill a fresh cache, then offline with the same call:

```python
import os, subprocess, sys, tempfile, textwrap

cache = tempfile.mkdtemp()
code = textwrap.dedent("""
    from diffusers import FluxTransformer2DModel
    m = FluxTransformer2DModel.from_pretrained("hf-internal-testing/tiny-flux-sharded", subfolder="transformer")
    print("loaded", sum(p.numel() for p in m.parameters()), "params")
""")
env = dict(os.environ, HF_HOME=cache)
subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-c", code], env=env, check=True)        # online: fills the cache
env["HF_HUB_OFFLINE"] = "1"
sys.exit(subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-c", code], env=env).returncode)  # offline: same call fails
```

Output on main @ da1d382: the online call prints `loaded 68484 params`. The offline call fails with the trace under Logs. With the fix below, the offline call also prints `loaded 68484 params`.

### Logs

```shell
loaded 68484 params
Could not reach the Hub (Cannot reach https://huggingface.co/api/models/hf-internal-testing/tiny-flux-sharded: offline mode is enabled. To disable it, please unset the `HF_HUB_OFFLINE` environment variable.). Using cached commit hash for 'hf-internal-testing/tiny-flux-sharded'.
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<string>", line 3, in <module>
  File ".../hugg

Both pipelines pass the default `adapter_conditioning_scale=1.0` to `MultiAdapter.forward`. `MultiAdapter.forward` converts that float to a scalar tensor and then iterates it, raising `TypeError: iteration over a 0-d tensor`. It also silently truncates when a scale list has the wrong length.

Duplicate check:
This exact default-scale failure was reported in closed issue https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/issues/6274 and still reproduces on this commit, so this is not a new finding.

Impact:
A documented/default multi-adapter call fails unless users know to pass a list. Wrong-length scale lists can silently skip adapters.

Reproduction:
```python
import torch
from diffusers import MultiAdapter, T2IAdapter

multi = MultiAdapter([
    T2IAdapter(in_channels=3, channels=[4], num_res_blocks=1, downscale_factor=2),
    T2IAdapter(in_channels=3, channels=[4], num_res_blocks=1, downscale_factor=2),
])
xs = [torch.randn(1, 3, 8, 8), torch.randn(1, 3, 8, 8)]

try:
    multi(xs, 1.0)
except Exception as e:
    print(type(e).__name__, str(e))

print("short list accepted:", multi(xs, [1.0])[0].shape)
```

Relevant precedent:
https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/blob/0f1abc4ae8b0eb2a3b40e82a310507281144c423/examples/community/pipeline_stable_diffusion_xl_controlnet_adapter.py#L1089-L1090

Suggested fix:
```python
if adapter_weights is None:
    adapter_weights = [1 / self.num_adapter] * self.num_adapter
elif isinstance(adapter_weights, (float, int)):
    adapter_weights = [float(adapter_weights)] * self.num_adapter
elif len(adapter_weights) != self.num_adapter:
    raise ValueError(
        f"`adapter_weights` must have length {self.num_adapter}, got {len(adapter_weights)}."
    )

if len(xs) != self.num_adapter:
    raise ValueError(f"`xs` must have length {self.num_adapter}, got {len(xs)}.")
```

## Issue 2: SDXL adapter pipeline does not accept `list[T2IAdapter]` despite its public signature

Affected code:
https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/blob/0f1abc4ae8b0eb2a3b40e82a310507281144c423/src/diffusers/pipelines/t2i_adapter/pipeline_stable_diffusion_xl_adapter.py#L273-L290

issues.title: `StateManager`, `Hook`, `State`: missing context setting (cond or uncond) in pipelines
issues.body:
In diffusion denoising model, we usually use `classifier free guidance` to control qualities. With [State Manager](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/blob/152f7ca357c066c4af3d1a58cdf17662ef5a2f87/src/diffusers/hooks/hooks.py#L42), we want each context hold different `state`, so we have to set which context when calling `self.transformer`, here is [a good example](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/blob/152f7ca357c066c4af3d1a58cdf17662ef5a2f87/src/diffusers/pipelines/hunyuan_image/pipeline_hunyuanimage.py#L797)

But some popular pipelines (Flux2) or pipeline variants (Kontext, Image to image, Inpainting) don't implement this. For example, [Flux T2I](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/blob/152f7ca357c066c4af3d1a58cdf17662ef5a2f87/src/diffusers/pipelines/flux/pipeline_flux.py#L943) has it while [Flux Kontext](https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/blob/152f7ca357c066c4af3d1a58cdf17662ef5a2f87/src/diffusers/pipelines/flux/pipeline_flux_kontext.py#L1088) is missing

A Fix should be simple but require us to check all pipelines
```python
with self.transformer.cache_context("cond"):
    noise_pred = self.transformer(...)
with self.transformer.cache_context("uncond"):
    neg_noise_pred = self.transformer(...)
```

issues.title: QwenImage21: model.to(bf16) (as in train_dreambooth_lora_qwenimage21.py) rounds the timestep-embedding freqs buffer, so LoRA training sees a different embedding than inference
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

`QwenImage21TemporalTimesteps` stores its sinusoid frequencies as a non-persistent `freqs` buffer and multiplies them by `1000 * t`, so the arguments reach about 1000 rad. `from_pretrained(torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16)` keeps the buffer in fp32, so inference is exact. But a later `model.to(dtype=torch.bfloat16)` rounds `freqs` to bf16 and shifts the high-frequency channels of the timestep embedding by up to about 1.4 rad.

The official LoRA script does exactly that. `examples/dreambooth/train_dreambooth_lora_qwenimage21.py` loads the transformer with `torch_dtype=weight_dtype` and then calls `transformer.to(device=accelerator.device, dtype=weight_dtype)`. So with `--mixed_precision bf16`, LoRAs are trained against a different timestep embedding than the one the inference pipeline uses.

The `timestep.float()` in `forward` doesn't help, because the buffer itself has already been rounded.

### Reproduction

CPU, tiny config, same load/cast sequence as the training script:

```python
import math, torch
from diffusers import QwenImage21Transformer2DModel

torch.manual_seed(0)
QwenImage21Transformer2DModel(
    num_layers=1, attention_head_dim=16, num_attention_heads=2, context_in_dim=32,
    in_channels=8, out_channels=8, axes_dims_rope=(4, 6, 6),
).save_pretrained("tiny-qwenimage21")

t = torch.linspace(0, 1, 1001)
half = 128
freqs = torch.exp(-math.log(10000) * torch.arange(half, dtype=torch.float32) / half)
args = (1000 * t)[:, None] * freqs[None]
reference = torch.cat([torch.cos(args), torch.sin(args)], dim=-1)  # exact fp32 embedding

inference = QwenImage21Transformer2DModel.from_pretrained("tiny-qwenimage21", torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16)
training = QwenImage21Transformer2DModel.from_pretrained("tiny-qwenimage21", torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16)
training.to(dtype=torch.bfloat16)  # what train_dreambooth_lora_qwenimage21.py does

for name, model in (("inference (from_pretrained)", inference), ("training (.to(dtype=bf16))", training)):
    proj = model.time_text_embed.time_proj
    emb = proj(t)
    angle = torch.atan2(emb[:, half:].double(), emb[:, :half].double())
    ref_angle = torch.atan2(reference[:, half:].double(), reference[:, :half].double())
    err = ((angle - ref_angle + math.pi) % (2 * math.pi) - math.pi).abs()
    print(f"{name:28s} freqs={proj.freqs.dtype}, max angle error {err.max():.3f} rad, "
          f"{(err > 0.1).float().mean() * 100:.1f}% of angles off by > 0.1 rad, "
          f"max |embedding diff| {(emb.float() - reference).abs().max():.3f}")
```

Output on `main` (8b33bfc):

```
inference (from_pretrained)  freqs=torch.float32, max angle error 0.000 rad, 0.0% of angles off by > 0.1 rad, max |embedding diff| 0.000
training (.to(dtype=bf16))   freqs=torch.bfloat16, max angle error 1.388 rad, 13.9% of angles off by > 0.1 rad, max |embedding diff| 1.272
```

### Suggested fix

Compute the frequencies in fp32 inside `forward`, as the generic `Timesteps` / `get_timestep_embedding` already does, instead of keeping them in a buffer. The buffer is non-persistent, so no checkpoint key changes:

```diff
     def __init__(self, timestep_dim: int, max_period: int = 10000, time_factor: float = 1000.0):
         super().__init__()
         self.timestep_dim = timestep_dim
         self.time_factor = time_factor
-        half = timestep_dim // 2
-        freqs = torch.exp(-math.log(max_period) * torch.arange(start=0, end=half, dtype=torch.float32) / h

issues.title: StableAudio3DiTModel: loading with torch_dtype=bf16/fp16 collapses RoPE positions (arange built in inv_freq dtype)
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

Loading `StableAudio3DiTModel` with `torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16` or `torch.float16` makes many audio-latent positions share the same rotary angle. That happens on the default load path, from roughly 30 s of audio in bf16 and roughly 3 min in fp16.

Two things combine in `StableAudio3RotaryEmbedding`:

1. `inv_freq` is registered with `persistent=True` (deliberately, to match the reference checkpoint key), so `from_pretrained(torch_dtype=...)` casts it to the requested dtype like any other state-dict tensor.
2. `forward` builds the **positions** in that dtype:
   ```python
   t = torch.arange(seq_len, device=device, dtype=self.inv_freq.dtype)
   freqs = torch.outer(t, self.inv_freq)
   ```
   bf16 represents integers exactly only up to 256 and fp16 only up to 2048. Beyond that, neighbouring positions round to the same value, and the rounded `inv_freq` adds a further error that grows with the position.

With the production config (`embed_dim=1536`, `num_heads=24` → rotary dim 32, 64 memory tokens, AutoencoderSAME's 44.1 kHz / 4096 → ~10.8 latents per second), measured against an fp32 reference:

| audio | seq_len | fp16: collapsed positions / angles off by > 0.1 rad | bf16: collapsed positions / angles off by > 0.1 rad |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10 s | 172 | 0 / 0.0% | 0 / 2.3% |
| 30 s | 387 | 0 / 0.6% | 65 / 9.2% |
| 47 s | 571 | 0 / 1.1% | 172 / 13.4% |
| 2 min | 1356 | 0 / 3.7% | 802 / 24.2% |
| ~3 min | 2110 | 31 / 6.6% | 1465 / 29.7% |
| 5 min | 3294 | 623 / 11.6% | 2575 / 35.0% |

The docs example (fp16, 10 s) is fine. Longer clips, and bf16 in general, are not.

### Reproduction

CPU, tiny config, public API only:

```python
import math, torch
from diffusers.models.transformers.transformer_stable_audio3 import StableAudio3DiTModel

torch.manual_seed(0)
StableAudio3DiTModel(
    io_channels=8, embed_dim=128, depth=1, num_heads=2, cond_token_dim=16, global_cond_dim=16,
    local_add_cond_dim=9, timestep_features_dim=16, num_memory_tokens=64,
).save_pretrained("tiny-sa3")

ref = StableAudio3DiTModel.from_pretrained("tiny-sa3").rotary_pos_emb  # fp32
for dtype in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16):
    rope = StableAudio3DiTModel.from_pretrained("tiny-sa3", torch_dtype=dtype).rotary_pos_emb
    for seconds in (30, 120):
        seq_len = 64 + math.ceil(seconds * 44100 / 4096)
        err = (rope(seq_len, "cpu").double() - ref(seq_len, "cpu").double() + math.pi).remainder(2 * math.pi) - math.pi
        positions = torch.arange(seq_len, dtype=rope.inv_freq.dtype)
        print(f"{str(dtype):15s} {seconds:4d}s: inv_freq={rope.inv_freq.dtype}, "
              f"collapsed positions {seq_len - positions.float().unique().numel()}/{seq_len}, "
              f"max angle error {err.abs().max():.2f} rad")
```

Output on `main` (8b33bfc):

```
torch.float16     30s: inv_freq=torch.float16, collapsed positions 0/387, max angle error 0.12 rad
torch.float16    120s: inv_freq=torch.float16, collapsed positions 0/1356, max angle error 0.46 rad
torch.bfloat16    30s: inv_freq=torch.bfloat16, collapsed positions 65/387, max angle error 1.12 rad
torch.bfloat16   120s: inv_freq=torch.bfloat16, collapsed positions 802/1356, max angle error 3.08 rad
```

### Suggested fix

I tested this locally:

```diff
 class StableAudio3RotaryEmbedding(nn.Module):
     def forward(self, seq_len: int, device: torch.device) -> torch.Tensor:
-        t = torch.arange(seq_len, device=device, d

issues.title: Expanded init fields in StableDiffusionPipeline cause incompatibilities with many/most inherited pipelines
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

class `StableDiffusionPipeline` has its init section as:
```py
    def __init__(
        self,
        vae: AutoencoderKL,
        text_encoder: CLIPTextModel,
        tokenizer: CLIPTokenizer,
        unet: UNet2DConditionModel,
        scheduler: KarrasDiffusionSchedulers,
        safety_checker: StableDiffusionSafetyChecker,
        feature_extractor: CLIPImageProcessor,
        image_encoder: CLIPVisionModelWithProjection = None,
        requires_safety_checker: bool = True,
    ):
```

and here `image_encoder` was recently introduced thus changing the class signature  
but most community pipelines do not include init field for recently included `image_encoder` and thus order or params is wrong  

for example, `examples/community/regional_prompting_stable_diffusion.py` has this in its init:  
```py
        super().__init__(
            vae,
            text_encoder,
            tokenizer,
            unet,
            scheduler,
            safety_checker,
            feature_extractor,
            requires_safety_checker,
        )
```
which means `bool` value from `requires_safety_checker` is going to be passed as `image_encoder` and pipeline will fail during initialization like this:  

```log
> diffusers/pipelines/pipeline_utils.py:546 in _fetch_class_library_tuple
AttributeError: 'bool' object has no attribute '__module__'
```

this is a conceptual problem with changing master class signature while all inherited classes pass args list as simple list.  
i don't see a simple solution as going back is bad and going forward requires updates to a lot of pipelines.  

but at the very basic, at least add error handling to `_fetch_class_library_tuple` so invalid type does not cause entire solution to crash.

### Reproduction

load nearly any community pipeline or any pipeline inherited from StableDiffusionPipeline, but not updated to use new signature in its `super().__init__` call

### Logs

_No response_

### System Info

diffusers==0.26.3

### Who can help?

@yiyixuxu @DN6 @sayakpaul @patrickvonplaten

issues.title: Suggestion for speeding up `index_for_timestep` by removing sequential `nonzero()` calls in samplers
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
First off, thanks for the great codebase and providing so many resources! I just wanted to provide some insight into an improvement I made for myself, in case you'd like to include it for all samplers. I'm using the `FlowMatchEulerDiscreteScheduler` and after profiling, I've noticed that it's unexpectedly slowing down my training speeds. I'll describe the issue and proposed solution here rather than making a PR, since this would touch a lot of code and perhaps someone on the diffusers team would like to implement it.

**Describe the solution you'd like.**
This line in particular is very slow because it is a for loop `step_indices = [self.index_for_timestep(t, schedule_timesteps) for t in timestep]` and the `self.index_for_timestep()` is calling a nonzero() function which is slow.

https://github.com/huggingface/diffusers/blob/b9e2f886cd6e9182f1bf1bf7421c6363956f94c5/src/diffusers/schedulers/scheduling_flow_match_euler_discrete.py#L149

**Describe alternatives you've considered.**
I've changed the code as follows:

```python
# huggingface code
def index_for_timestep(self, timestep, schedule_timesteps=None):
    if schedule_timesteps is None:
        schedule_timesteps = self.timesteps

    indices = (schedule_timesteps == timestep).nonzero()

    # The sigma index that is taken for the **very** first `step`
    # is always the second index (or the last index if there is only 1)
    # This way we can ensure we don't accidentally skip a sigma in
    # case we start in the middle of the denoising schedule (e.g. for image-to-image)
    pos = 1 if len(indices) > 1 else 0

    return indices[pos].item()
```

changed to =>

```python
# my code
def index_for_timestep(self, timestep, schedule_timesteps=None):
    if schedule_timesteps is None:
        schedule_timesteps = self.timesteps

    num_steps = len(schedule_timesteps)
    start = schedule_timesteps[0].item()
    end = schedule_timesteps[-1].item()
    indices = torch.round(((timestep - start) / (end - start)) * (num_steps - 1)).long()

    return indices
```

and

```python
# huggingface code
# self.begin_index is None when scheduler is used for training, or pipeline does not implement set_begin_index
if self.begin_index is None:
    step_indices = [self.index_for_timestep(t, schedule_timesteps) for t in timestep]
```

changed to =>

```python
# my code
# self.begin_index is None when scheduler is used for training, or pipeline does not implement set_begin_index
if self.begin_index is None:
    step_indices = self.index_for_timestep(timestep, schedule_timesteps)
```

**Additional context.**
Just wanted to bring this modification to your attention since it could be a training speedup for folks. 🙂 Especially when someone has a large batch size > 1 and this for loop it occurring with nonzero search operations. Some other small changes might be necessary to ensure compatibility of the function changes, but I suspect it could help everyone. Thanks for the consideration!

positioning.overview:
FastVideo 是一个面向视频生成大模型（如 Wan2.1/2.2, MiniMax-H3 等 DiT 架构）的端到端统一推理与后训练（Post-training）加速框架。它的核心价值在于打破了“训练”与“推理”的壁垒，通过算法层（DMD2 蒸馏、Video Sparse Attention 稀疏注意力、Self-Forcing 因果蒸馏）与系统层（定制 CUDA/Triton 算子、序列并行、Attn-QAT 量化）的深度协同，实现了极速甚至实时的视频生成（如其内置的 Dreamverse 实时流应用）。目前项目处于高速迭代与多硬件平台扩展期（正向 0.2.x 版本演进，近期密集提交了对 Apple Silicon、DGX Spark 和 ROCm 的支持）。

针对你的硬约束（仅有一台 16GB Apple Silicon MacBook Air，无本地 NVIDIA GPU）：虽然你擅长 CUDA/Triton 和高端 GPU 性能优化，但由于缺乏本地验证环境，直接开发前沿 CUDA 算子（如仓库中已出现的 `sm100a` 或 FP8 算子）会非常痛苦，Colab 免费 T4（仅支持 sm75）无法验证这些新特性。你的最佳切入路径有两条：第一，发挥你的端侧部署与量化经验，深耕 `fastvideo/mlx_runtime` 目录，为 FastMetal-QAD 模型编写或优化基于 Apple Metal 的底层算子，这完全可以在你的 Mac 上本地闭环；第二，发挥你的分布式训练性能经验，在纯 CPU 环境下开发和单测 `fastvideo/distributed` 中的 Sequence Parallelism（序列并行）切分逻辑或 FSDP2 调度策略，仅在最终提交前用 Colab T4 做几十分钟的集成冒烟测试。
positioning.problem: 开源视频生成大模型（DiT）面临计算量巨大、显存占用极高、推理极慢的痛点，难以在消费级硬件或端侧实时运行；同时，社区缺乏一个将数据预处理、微调、稀疏化蒸馏（DMD2）、量化感知训练（QAT）与高性能推理后端无缝打通的开箱即用框架。FastVideo 旨在为 AI 研究员和应用开发者提供一站式解决方案，典型场景包括：1) 对开源 DiT 模型进行稀疏蒸馏以获得 50x 加速；2) 在多卡环境部署长视频的序列并行推理服务；3) 在 Apple Silicon Mac 上本地运行 FastMetal-QAD 模型；4) 部署 Dreamverse 实现“Vibe Directing”实时互动视频生成。
positioning.users: 视频生成模型算法研究员（需快速验证蒸馏/稀疏化算法）、AI 视频应用开发者（需接入高性能 API 或部署实时视频流）、以及希望在本地（如 Mac 或单张 4090）运行视频生成的端侧极客。

landscape.difference: Diffusers 是基础模型库，FastVideo 依赖它（diffusers>=0.38.0），但 FastVideo 提供了更激进的系统级定制（如独立编译的 fastvideo-kernel、序列并行）和后训练算法（DMD2、VSA），推理速度远超原生 Diffusers。
vLLM 等主要面向 LLM 和 VLM 的文本/图像推理。FastVideo 专注于视频生成（DiT 架构），包含时间维度的特殊处理（如 Video Sparse Attention）以及完整的后训练（微调/蒸馏）闭环。
偏向通用的底层大模型预训练框架。FastVideo 专注于视频生成的“后训练”阶段，集成了 FSDP2 和针对 DiT 优化的序列并行，且直接与推理后端对齐。

positioning.stage: 高速发展与多平台扩展期（已发布 V1，正向 0.2.x 迭代，近期高频提交 Apple Silicon、DGX Spark、ROCm 支持及新模型适配）。

positioning.numbers: 核心代码库 fastvideo 包含 1353 个文件，examples 319 个文件，apps 308 个文件，tests 164 个文件，定制算子库 fastvideo-kernel 105 个文件。近期提交极其频繁（如 2026年9月14日-18日期间有大量 bugfix 和 perf 提交），提交热点集中在 docs/cookbook (17)、fastvideo/tests (11) 和 fastvideo/pipelines (6)。已发布 0.1.6, 0.1.7, 0.2.0 等多个 Release。

codemap.layers:
FastVideo 的架构设计高度模块化，旨在打破训练与推理的壁垒，同时兼顾前沿 GPU 算力与端侧部署。针对你的硬约束（仅有 Mac），整体架构可划分为五层，其中有两层是你绝佳的切入点：

1. **应用与入口层 (Application & Entrypoints)**：最上层是面向最终用户的应用（如 `apps/dreamverse` 实时流应用和 `apps/fastvideo_studio` 任务管理 UI），以及面向开发者的 Python API 入口（`fastvideo/entrypoints/video_generator.py`）。这一层负责接收用户 Prompt、解析配置（`fastvideo/api`），并统筹整个生成任务。
2. **调度与管线层 (Pipeline & Distributed Scheduling)**：核心控制中枢。`fastvideo/pipelines` 负责管理扩散模型的去噪循环（Denoising Loop）、CFG 缩放等算法逻辑；`fastvideo/distributed` 负责多卡环境下的 Sequence Parallelism（序列并行）切分与 FSDP2 调度。**对于只有 Mac 的你，这里的分布式切分逻辑完全可以在纯 CPU 环境下开发和单测，是绝佳的切入点。**
3. **模型层 (Models)**：位于 `fastvideo/models`，定义了各种 DiT 架构（如 Wan2.1/2.2, MiniMax-H3, FLUX 等）的组网逻辑。这里将 Transformer Block 的计算图与底层的具体算子解耦。
4. **执行路由层 (Execution Routing)**：位于 `fastvideo/attention`。这是一个高度抽象的注意力后端路由层（如 `backends/abstract.py`），根据当前硬件环境和配置，动态将 Attention 计算分发给最合适的底层实现（如 FlashAttn, SageAttn, BSA, 或 MLX）。
5. **硬件与 Kernel 层 (Hardware & Kernels)**：性能压榨的极地。包含针对 NVIDIA GPU 的 `fastvideo-kernel`（如 `sm100a` 块稀疏算子、`attn_qat_infer` 量化算子），以及针对 Apple Silicon 的 `fastvideo/mlx_runtime`。**由于你缺乏本地 NVIDIA GPU，深耕 `mlx_runtime`，为 FastMetal-QAD 编写基于 Metal 的底层算子，将是你发挥端侧部署与量化经验、且能在本地完美闭环的最佳战场。**

codemap.data_flow:
以一次典型的端到端视频生成请求（如执行 `examples/inference/basic/basic_wan2_2_i2v.py`）为例，数据流转如下：

1. **请求初始化与配置解析**：用户通过 `VideoGenerator.from_pretrained()` 实例化生成器。系统进入 `fastvideo/api`，解析 `SamplingParam`（如步数、CFG、分辨率）和 `PipelineConfig`。此时，系统会探测硬件环境。如果在 Apple Silicon 上，会自动将后端指向 MLX；如果在多卡 GPU 上，则初始化 NCCL/MPI 环境。
2. **分布式策略构建（CPU 调度点）**：如果启用了序列并行（Sequence Parallelism），请求会进入 `fastvideo/distributed`。在这里，长视频的 Latent Tensor 会在 CPU 层面被逻辑切分，计算出每张卡的通信拓扑和切片索引（**你可以在 Mac 上通过 Mock 进程数来单测这部分逻辑**）。
3. **去噪管线执行**：进入 `fastvideo/pipelines`。管线根据 DMD2 蒸馏或标准 ODE 求解器，启动 Denoising Loop。每一步迭代，Latent Tensor 和条件特征（Text/Image Embeddings）被送入 `fastvideo/models` 中的 DiT Block。
4. **注意力计算路由**：在 DiT Block 内部，遇到最耗时的 Attention 计算时，调用 `fastvideo/attention/backends/abstract.py`。路由层根据配置（如 `FASTVIDEO_ATTENTION_BACKEND` 环境变量）将张量派发。
5. **底层 Kernel 执行**：
   - **Mac 本地路径**：请求路由至 `fastvideo/mlx_runtime`，调用基于 Apple Metal 优化的 QAD（Quantization-Aware Distillation）算子，完成低比特矩阵乘法与注意力计算。
   - **GPU 路径**：请求路由至 `fastvideo-kernel`，调用如 `attn_qat_infer`（FP4/FP8 量化注意力）或 `block_sparse_attn`（VSA 稀疏注意力）的 CUDA/Triton 算子。
6. **解码与输出**：去噪循环结束后，最终的 Latent Tensor 通过 VAE 解码为像素级视频帧，封装为 `VideoResult` 返回，或通过 `apps/dreamverse` 的 WebSocket 实时推流给前端。

extension_points.how: 新模型接入：在 models 目录下新建模型文件实现 DiT 架构，并在 registry.py 中注册模型路径与 Workload 类型。

新 Apple Silicon 算子：在此目录下添加 Metal 实现，这是你在 Mac 上本地闭环优化的核心扩展点。
新 CUDA/Triton 算子：编写 C++ 或 Triton 代码，并在 fastvideo-kernel/CMakeLists.txt 中配置编译。
新调度策略：添加新的切分逻辑（如新的 FSDP2 包装器或序列并行通信组），纯 CPU 编写单测验证。

diagram.caption: FastVideo 架构图：从顶层 API 到底层硬件算子的完整调用链路，展示了高度解耦的路由机制。

install: git clone https://github.com/hao-ai-lab/FastVideo.git
cd FastVideo
uv venv --python 3.12 --seed
source .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install -e '.[mlx,dev]'
pre-commit install --hook-type pre-commit --hook-type commit-msg
runbook.no_gpu_paths:
1. **完全可在 Mac (CPU/Metal) 闭环**：`fastvideo/mlx_runtime/`（Apple Silicon 专属算子与推理后端，这是你发挥端侧部署经验的主战场）；`fastvideo/distributed/`（序列并行与 FSDP2 的切分逻辑，纯 CPU 即可开发与单测）；`fastvideo/pipelines/` 与 `fastvideo/models/`（计算图构建与调度逻辑）。
2. **只能读代码或用 Colab T4 验证**：`fastvideo-kernel/` 下的 CUDA/Triton 算子。注意，T4 仅支持 sm75，仓库中前沿的 `sm100a` (Blackwell)、FP8 (`fp8_wan2_1_1_3b.py`)、NVFP4 (`nvfp4_qat_wan2_1_1_3b.py`) 算子在 T4 上**绝对无法运行**，只能做最基础的 Triton 算子冒烟测试。`pyproject.toml` 中已通过 `sys_platform == 'linux'` 巧妙屏蔽了 Mac 上的 `fastvideo-kernel` 和 `flashinfer-python` 编译，因此本地不会报错。
smoke_test: python examples/inference/basic/mlx_wan_prompt_to_video.py
python examples/inference/basic/mlx_fasth3.py
python examples/inference/basic/mlx_wan_decode_benchmark.py
FASTVIDEO_ATTENTION_BACKEND=SDPA python examples/inference/basic/basic.py
pytest fastvideo/tests/ -k 'distributed'
runbook.test_suite: 测试框架为 `pytest`。主要目录分为 `fastvideo/tests/` (包级别测试) 和 `tests/local_tests/` (本地组件测试)。**CPU 子集跑法**：运行 `pytest fastvideo/tests/ --ignore=fastvideo/tests/ssim/`。根据 `AGENTS.md` 明确指出，`ssim/` 目录包含重度依赖 GPU 的画质回归测试，在 Mac 上必须跳过。纯 CPU/MLX 测试耗时通常在几分钟内。
debug_tips: 环境变量：设置 FASTVIDEO_ATTENTION_BACKEND=MLX 或 SDPA，强制在 Mac 上走非 CUDA 注意力后端（参考 fastvideo/attention/backends/ 路由逻辑）。
日志开关：项目使用 loguru（见 pyproject.toml），可通过设置 LOGURU_LEVEL=DEBUG 开启底层详细日志。
Profiling 入口：参考 examples/inference/basic/basic_fasth3_simplified_profile.py，结合 fastvideo/profiler.py 进行性能分析。
断点调试：由于涉及多进程分布式逻辑 (FSDP2/SP)，推荐使用 pyproject.toml 中引入的 remote-pdb 进行分布式断点，或在纯 CPU 单测中使用标准 pdb。
runbook.ci: CI 结合了 GitHub Actions (`.github/workflows/`) 与 Buildkite (`.buildkite/pipeline.yml`，用于 performance-benchmarks)。PR 会被严格的 `pre-commit` 钩子卡住（包含 yapf, ruff, mypy, codespell）。此外，涉及模型输出的修改会被 GPU 节点上的 SSIM 画质回归测试卡住。
pitfalls: **格式化工具绕过陷阱**：AGENTS.md 强烈警告，不要直接运行 yapf/ruff/mypy，必须通过 pre-commit 运行。如果 pre-commit 提示 fastvideo/tests/ '(no files to check)'，这是 .pre-commit-config.yaml 故意排除的，绝不要手动绕过。
**Mac 编译 Kernel 陷阱**：千万不要在 Mac 上手贱执行 `cd fastvideo-kernel && ./build.sh`，它无条件调用 nvcc 会直接报错。正常 uv pip install 时，pyproject.toml 里的 sys_platform == 'linux' 已经帮你安全跳过了 CUDA 依赖。
**依赖版本陷阱**：不要随意升级 tokenizers。pyproject.toml 明确注释 tokenizers 必须 <0.23，否则会因为 RobertaProcessing 绑定参数重命名导致 CLIP 风格的 tokenizer 加载崩溃。
**Colab T4 算力陷阱**：不要试图在 Colab T4 上验证 fastvideo-kernel/attn_qat_infer/blackwell/ 或 sm100a 相关的代码，T4 (sm75) 硬件不支持，强行跑只会得到 CUDA error。

community.cadence: 仓库处于高速迭代期。近期提交非常密集（如 2026年9月14日至18日每天都有多个 Commit 合并）。Release 频率大约每 4-5 个月发布一次大版本（证据：0.1.6 于 2025-08-29，0.1.7 于 2026-01-05，0.2.0 于 2026-06-04）。

community.process: 贡献流程规范严格：1. 重大变更或讨论需先提交带有 `[RFC]:` 标签的 Issue（如 #1374, #1606）。2. 本地开发强依赖 pre-commit，必须执行 `pre-commit install --hook-type pre-commit --hook-type commit-msg`。3. PR 必须包含明确的测试证据（`pytest` 或 SSIM 输出，若跳过需说明理由），并关联相关 Issue。4. Commit 信息需遵循 `[tag]: subject (#PR)` 格式（如 `[bugfix]: ...`, `[feat]: ...`）。
community.review_style: 务实且高度关注性能与回归测试。从 `AGENTS.md` 要求 PR 必须提供 SSIM/pytest 证据，以及 #1374 专门追踪性能回归可以看出，Review 过程会严格把关代码对生成质量和推理速度的影响。响应速度快，近期 Issue（如 #1850, #1834）均有快速跟进和指派。
etiquette: 得体：使用 `uv` 管理虚拟环境（README 强烈推荐）；在 PR 中提供明确的测试证据（pytest/SSIM）；在需要特定硬件的测试中明确记录 GPU 假设。
不得体：直接调用 `yapf`/`ruff`/`mypy` 绕过 `pre-commit` 的配置；强行检查被 `.pre-commit-config.yaml` 故意排除的文件（如 `fastvideo/tests/`，AGENTS.md 明确警告不要 bypass）；提交没有 tag 前缀的 Commit。
what_they_want: 急需社区贡献的特性：Issue #960 `[Feature] Log-linear Sparse Attention` (标记了 help wanted, good first issue) 和 Issue #775 `[Feature] TDM` (标记了 contribution-needed)。

结合你的背景（端侧/量化/分布式），维护者目前非常需要 Issue #1822 `Support FSDP inference with precomputed quantized weights` 以及 Issue #1821 `Support LoRA lifecycle operations for MXFP8 and NVFP4 inference` 方面的帮助，这与你的技能树完美契合，且 FSDP 逻辑可在 Mac 上纯 CPU 单测闭环。
2026 Q3 Roadmap (#1603) 相关的持续演进（需验证具体 Roadmap 内容，但明确在招募贡献）。

gaps.gap: Apple Silicon (MLX) 后端的算子性能与显存优化（如针对 16GB 内存的极致 Offload）
gaps.evidence: 仓库近期密集增加了对 Apple Silicon 的支持（如 `fastvideo/mlx_runtime` 目录，以及 README 中提到的 FastMetal-QAD 模型），且最近的 Commit（如 `[perf] H3 decode: offload the frozen VAEs`）显示团队正在高度关注显存 Offload 优化。
gaps.why_you: 你拥有 16GB Mac，这是复现端侧显存瓶颈的绝佳环境；你的端侧部署与量化经验（TensorRT/量化）可以降维打击，将 CUDA/Triton 的显存复用与算子融合思想迁移到 Metal/MLX 上。

gaps.gap: 分布式切分逻辑（Sequence Parallelism / FSDP2）的纯 CPU 单元测试与 Mock
gaps.evidence: 项目包含 `fastvideo/distributed` 目录，且测试套件中有 `pytest fastvideo/tests/ -k 'distributed'`。但分布式逻辑通常强依赖多 GPU 环境，缺乏在纯 CPU 下验证切分拓扑和通信原语（如 `ulysses_all_to_all` 的 Python 侧 Mock）的测试。
gaps.why_you: 你精通分布式训练性能，完全可以在不依赖 GPU 的情况下，在 Mac 上用纯 PyTorch CPU 编写张量切分、形状推导和通信路由的单测，保障核心逻辑的鲁棒性。

gaps.gap: Attention 路由层在无 GPU 环境下的优雅降级与 SDPA 对齐
gaps.evidence: `fastvideo/attention/backends/` 目录下有 `abstract.py`、`flash_attn.py`、`sdpa.py` 等。目前前沿算子（如 `attn_qat_infer`）强依赖 CUDA，缺乏在 CPU/Mac 上使用标准 SDPA 进行数学等价性验证的机制。
gaps.why_you: 你熟悉 PyTorch 内核与算子融合，能够编写高精度的 CPU SDPA 对照组，用于在 CI 中验证 QAT（量化感知训练）或 VSA（视频稀疏注意力）的数学正确性。

gaps.why_you: 你精通 Triton，知道如何将 Triton 的 Block/Grid 逻辑抽象为纯 Python 循环或 CPU 张量操作，从而在 Mac 上验证索引计算（Index Math）的正确性。

gaps.gap: 端侧量化模型（FastMetal-QAD）的性能 Benchmark 脚本完善
gaps.evidence: `examples/inference/basic/` 下有 `mlx_wan_decode_benchmark.py` 和 `mlx_wan_quant_benchmark.py`，但端侧性能看板（Dashboard）和自动化回归追踪仍需加强（Issue #1374 追踪性能回归）。
gaps.why_you: 你擅长性能工程，可以在本地 Mac 上完善这些 Benchmark 脚本，增加对显存峰值（Peak Memory）和吞吐量（Tokens/s）的精确统计。

entry.ownership_target: fastvideo/mlx_runtime (Apple Silicon 推理后端) 与 fastvideo/distributed (分布式调度逻辑)
entry.why_this_target: 这是在你的硬约束（仅有 16GB Mac，无本地 NVIDIA GPU）下，唯一能通向核心 Maintainer 的双轨路径。一方面，`mlx_runtime` 是你发挥端侧部署与量化经验的主战场，你可以将 CUDA 算子优化的思想降维应用到 Metal 上，且完全在本地闭环测试；另一方面，`distributed` 目录下的序列并行（Sequence Parallelism）和 FSDP2 调度本质上是计算图切分与通信拓扑设计，纯 CPU 即可完成逻辑开发与单测。这两个模块既是当前项目高速扩张的核心（见近期 MLX 和 Spark 的密集提交），又能完美避开你无法运行 `sm100a` 或 FP8 CUDA 算子的硬件劣势。
phase_30: 阅读 `AGENTS.md` 和 `CONTRIBUTING`，严格按照规范配置本地开发环境：`uv venv --python 3.12`，`uv pip install -e '.[mlx,dev]'`。
必须执行 `pre-commit install --hook-type pre-commit --hook-type commit-msg`，确保本地代码风格（yapf/ruff/mypy）与 CI 完全一致。
在 Mac 上运行 `python examples/inference/basic/mlx_wan_prompt_to_video.py`，跑通 FastMetal-QAD 的端到端生成，观察 16GB 内存的占用情况。
精读 `fastvideo/attention/backends/abstract.py` 和 `fastvideo/mlx_runtime/` 目录，理解 FastVideo 是如何将 Attention 计算路由到 MLX 后端的。
精读 `fastvideo/distributed/` 目录，梳理 Sequence Parallelism 的张量切分逻辑。
在 GitHub Issue 中寻找带有 `[bugfix]` 或 `[test]` 标签的 MLX/CPU 相关问题，提交你的第一个 PR（如补充分布式逻辑的纯 CPU 单元测试）。
加入 Slack 和微信群（见 README 社区链接），自我介绍为专注于 Apple Silicon (MLX) 优化和分布式逻辑的贡献者。
phase_60: 使用 Mac 本地的性能分析工具（如 Instruments 或 MLX 自带 profiler）对 `mlx_wan_decode_benchmark.py` 进行 Profiling，定位显存或计算瓶颈。
参考近期 Commit `[perf] H3 decode: offload the frozen VAEs`，为 `mlx_runtime` 实现或优化针对 16GB 内存的极致 Offload 策略。
为 `fastvideo/distributed` 编写纯 CPU 的 Mock 测试，验证多卡环境下的 Token 切分与 Gather 逻辑，确保在无 GPU 环境下 CI 也能拦截分布式 Bug。
在 Colab T4 上进行几十分钟的冒烟测试，验证你对 `fastvideo/pipelines` 或 `fastvideo/models` 的修改没有破坏基础的 PyTorch (SDPA) 推理链路。
参与 `fastvideo/mlx_runtime` 相关 PR 的 Code Review，从端侧部署和量化的角度提供专业意见。
参加 Weekly Dev Meeting（通过 Discussions #982 追踪），分享你在 16GB Mac 上运行 1.3B/5B 模型的显存优化经验。
phase_90: 主导 `fastvideo/mlx_runtime` 的性能演进路线，例如将 Video Sparse Attention (VSA) 的核心逻辑用 MLX/Metal 高效实现，缩小与 CUDA 版本的性能差距。
重构 `fastvideo/distributed` 中的通信原语抽象，使其能更好地支持异构环境（如未来可能的跨 Mac 集群推理）。
向核心维护者（如 Davids048 或 macthecadillac）申请 `fastvideo/mlx_runtime` 和 `fastvideo/distributed` 目录的 Reviewer 权限。
撰写一篇关于“如何在 FastVideo 中为 Apple Silicon 编写高性能算子”的 Cookbook 文档，合并到 `docs/cookbook/` 中。

risks.risk: 在修改 `fastvideo/models` 或 `fastvideo/pipelines` 时，无意中破坏了前沿 CUDA 算子（如 `sm100a` 或 FP8）的调用逻辑，且本地无法测试。
risks.mitigation: 严格遵守架构的解耦设计，所有修改必须通过 `fastvideo/attention/backends/abstract.py` 路由。提交 PR 前，务必在 Colab T4 上运行 `FASTVIDEO_ATTENTION_BACKEND=SDPA python examples/inference/basic/basic.py` 进行基础冒烟测试，并依赖 CI 的 GPU 矩阵进行最终把关。

risks.risk: 本地代码风格检查失败，导致 PR 被 CI 拒绝。
risks.mitigation: 绝对不要绕过 pre-commit。必须执行 `pre-commit install`，并在提交前运行 `pre-commit run --all-files`。注意 `pyproject.toml` 中配置了 120 行宽限制，且 `.pre-commit-config.yaml` 有特定的 exclude 规则（如跳过 `fastvideo/tests/`），尊重这些既有规则。

risks.risk: 16GB Mac 显存在运行 DiT 模型时频繁 OOM，导致本地开发受阻。
risks.mitigation: 在开发初期，使用最小的模型（如 FastMetal-1.3B-QAD），或者在代码中编写 Mock 脚本，用随机初始化的极小 Shape 张量（如 1x4x16x16）来验证 MLX 算子逻辑，而不是每次都加载完整权重。

risks.risk: 试图在 Colab T4 上验证前沿特性（如 NVFP4 或 Blackwell 稀疏算子）导致挫败。
risks.mitigation: 明确认知 T4 仅支持 sm75。绝不碰 `fastvideo-kernel/csrc/` 下的 `sm100a` 或 `fp8` 代码。Colab T4 仅用于验证纯 PyTorch 逻辑、Triton 算子的基础 Fallback 以及 Gradio/API 层的连通性。

risks.risk: 项目迭代速度极快（每天多个 Commit），本地分支容易与 `main` 产生严重冲突。
risks.mitigation: 保持高频的 `git pull --rebase upstream main`。在开发新特性前，先在 Issue 中提交带有 `[RFC]:` 标签的方案，与维护者对齐后再动手，避免闭门造车导致代码废弃。

issues.title: [perf] Reuse cached VAE offload for H3 reference and keyframe encoding
issues.body:
Follow-up to #1867: use the retained VAE host-weight cache for MiniMax-H3 input encoding as well as output decoding.

The H3 decoding stages use `pinned_offload.load()` and `pinned_offload.unload()`. In
`fastvideo/pipelines/basic/minimax_h3/stages/minimax_h3_latent_preparation.py`,
`_encode_fl2va_conditions()` (keyframes) and `_encode_ref2va_conditions()` (reference media) still load the video VAE
with `.to(device)` and unload it with `.to("cpu")`. The reference-audio branch uses the same transfer pattern.

On CUDA, with `vae_cpu_offload=True` and `lazy_module_load=False`, a previous decode can leave a CPU weight cache.
When a later request encodes keyframes or reference media, `.to("cpu")` allocates another complete CPU weight copy
while that cache remains alive. Both copies coexist during the following denoising stage. For the full video VAE,
this adds approximately 10.4 GB of logical weight storage per participating rank, with pinning enabled or disabled.

Requested change:

- Route video VAE loading and unloading in both input-encoding functions through the helper introduced by #1867.
- Use the same mechanism for the audio VAE when encoding reference audio.
- Preserve `vae_cpu_offload` and `pin_cpu_memory` behavior and the existing cleanup on exceptions.

Validation:

- Exercise decode followed by reference or keyframe encoding on the same VAE with CPU offload enabled and lazy loading
  disabled, covering `pin_cpu_memory=True` and `False`.
- Verify that unloading restores parameters and buffers to the retained host storage without another full CPU copy.
- Verify that encoded values remain unchanged and that disabling CPU offload preserves GPU residency.

This follow-up covers input-encoding integration. The temporary memory peak while first constructing pinned storage
is accepted for #1867 and is outside this issue's scope. No encoding-upload speedup has been measured here.

issues.title: Support LoRA lifecycle operations for MXFP8 and NVFP4 inference
issues.body:
## Summary

MXFP8 and NVFP4 inference quantize transformer weights after merging the constructor-provided LoRA adapter. LoRA lifecycle operations must update those quantized weights before the next inference request.

PR #1796 rejects lifecycle operations that cannot maintain this invariant. This issue tracks implementing those operations.

Review context: https://github.com/hao-ai-lab/FastVideo/pull/1796#discussion_r3939549798

## Behavior implemented by PR #1796

| Public operation | MXFP8 | Default NVFP4 | NVFP4 with retained BF16 weights |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| unmerge_lora_weights() | Explicitly rejected | Explicitly rejected | Explicitly rejected |
| set_lora_adapter() | Allowed and requantized | Explicitly rejected | Allowed and requantized |

## Required work

- Support MXFP8 LoRA unmerge by quantizing the restored BF16 weights before inference.
- Support NVFP4 LoRA unmerge by preserving or restoring the BF16 weights and then quantizing the restored weights.
- Support default NVFP4 adapter changes by preserving or restoring the BF16 weights, merging the requested adapter, and then quantizing the merged weights.
- Keep quantized weights synchronized after every merge, unmerge, adapter change, strength change, and accumulated adapter update.

## Tests

- Verify MXFP8 unmerge and remerge behavior.
- Verify NVFP4 unmerge with both removed and retained BF16 weights.
- Verify adapter replacement for MXFP8 and NVFP4.
- Compare lifecycle outputs against the equivalent BF16 LoRA execution.

linked_prs.title: [feat] add MXFP8 support on H3
[bugfix]: requantize MXFP8 weights after LoRA unmerge

issues.title: [Bug] [ui/studio] Studio becomes unclickable after dismissing Create Job or creating a job
issues.body:
## Describe the bug

Studio can stop responding to clicks after using **Create Job**, both when dismissing the form and when successfully creating a job. The form disappears, but sidebar navigation and other controls remain unclickable until the page is refreshed.

After successful creation, the new job can appear in the queue while its **Start** button does not respond.

**Expected:** dismissing or submitting Create Job restores normal page interaction, and a newly created pending job can be started without refreshing.

**Actual:** the form is gone, but the page remains unclickable.

## Reproduction

### Dismiss the form

1. Open **Inference** and refresh to start with a responsive page.
2. Click **Create Job → T2V**.
3. Close the job-configuration form with **X**, without submitting it.
4. Click **Finetuning** in the sidebar. Navigation does not occur.

Also reproduced with **Finetuning → Create Job → Full** and **Distillation → Create Job → DMD**. This path needs no model selection or GPU execution.

### Submit successfully

1. Open **Create Job**, choose a workload, and enter a valid configuration. Disable automatic start when testing the Start button.
2. Submit the form and wait for the new pending job to appear.
3. Click **Start** or a sidebar navigation link. The page can remain unresponsive until refresh.

The successful-submission symptom was also reported during manual use; the dismissal path was independently reproduced across all three job pages.

### Evidence

After dismissal, browser inspection showed:

```json
{"pointerEvents": "none", "dialogs": 0, "menus": 0}
```

`body.style.pointerEvents` remains `none` although no dialog or menu is open. As a control, opening an existing job with **View** and closing it restored normal interaction. Refreshing is a workaround.

The dropdown and dialog resolve separate copies of Radix's dismissable-layer dependency, matching the dependency-coordination problem described in [Radix #1241](https://github.com/radix-ui/primitives/issues/1241#issuecomment-1298554059).

## Environment

- Initial reproduction: Google Chrome on macOS 26.6.2, September 14, 2026.

issues.title: [Bug] fastvideo-kernel build.sh --rocm cannot configure in the rocm/pytorch 7.14.1 image
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

`fastvideo-kernel/build.sh --rocm` cannot configure inside the official `rocm/pytorch:rocm7.14.1_ubuntu24.04_py3.12_pytorch_release_2.12.0` image. CMake cannot enable the HIP language: that image installs ROCm as the pip-packaged SDK (`_rocm_sdk_core` inside the venv), which carries `hipcc` but no `hip-lang` CMake package, and there is no `/opt/rocm`. So on AMD GPUs using the stock image there is currently no supported way to install `fastvideo_kernel`, even though the sparse attention path only needs its Python and Triton modules.

### Reproduction

No model is involved; this is the kernel package build.

```bash
cd fastvideo-kernel
./build.sh --rocm
```

```
-- The CXX compiler identification is GNU 13.3.0
-- The HIP compiler identification is unknown
-- Configuring incomplete, errors occurred!
CMake Error at .../cmake/data/share/cmake-4.4/Modules/CMakeDetermineHIPCompiler.cmake:257 (message):
  The ROCm root directory:

   /opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/_rocm_sdk_core

  does not contain the HIP runtime CMake package, expected at one of:

   /opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/_rocm_sdk_core/lib/cmake/hip-lang/hip-lang-config.cmake
   /opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/_rocm_sdk_core/lib64/cmake/hip-lang/hip-lang-config.cmake
   /opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/_rocm_sdk_core/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/cmake/hip-lang/hip-lang-config.cmake

Call Stack (most recent call first):
  CMakeLists.txt:20 (enable_language)
```

On that image `/opt/rocm` does not exist, `ROCM_PATH` is unset, and `_rocm_sdk_core/` contains `bin/` (`hipcc`, `hipify-clang`, `amd-smi`), `include/`, `lib/` and `share/`, but no `lib/cmake`.

### Environment

- AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950), Daytona sandbox
- `rocm/pytorch:rocm7.14.1_ubuntu24.04_py3.12_pytorch_release_2.12.0`: torch `2.12.0+rocm7.14.1`, HIP runtime 7.14.60850, Python 3.12.3, Ubuntu 24.04.4
- FastVideo `37d06a8`; `cmake` 4.4.3 and `scikit-build-core` 1.0.3 from PyPI

### What does work

The package itself works on ROCm once it is importable. With `PYTHONPATH=fastvideo-kernel/python` and no build, `import fastvideo_kernel` (0.3.5), `block_sparse_attn_256` and `triton_kernels.index` all import, and the Triton block-sparse attention runs on the MI355X:

```
block_sparse_attn first call (Triton autotune+compile) 16.1s -> (1, 4, 2048, 128) torch.bfloat16
vs masked fp32 SDPA: max abs diff 0.0014, mean 0.00011, ref mean abs 0.0519
sparse (10%) H=24 S=262144 D=128: 221.3 ms/call = 382 effective TFLOPS
dense flash SDPA same shape: 702.2 ms/call = 1203 TFLOPS -> sparse speedup 3.17x at 10% density
```

The same holds with `FASTVIDEO_VSA_TRITON=0`, i.e. the default dispatch also lands on Triton there. The fused block-mean and top-k kernels, `video_sparse_attn` as the Wan VSA backend calls it, and the 256-token tile path of `block_sparse_attn_256_bshd` also match PyTorch references on the same device.

### Suggestion

An install mode that skips the compiled extension would let `pip install ./fastvideo-kernel` ship the Python and Triton modules on ROCm: for example a CMake option that bypasses `enable_language(HIP)` and the extension targets when `GPU_BACKEND=ROCM` and the HIP toolchain is not found, or an explicit `FASTVIDEO_KERNEL_BUILD_EXTENSION=OFF`. Documenting `PYTHONPATH=fastvideo-kernel/python` as the interim route would also help. Happy to send a PR for whichever you prefer.

Related: #1849 fixes ROCm platform detection in the same image.

issues.title: [Feature] Add Dreamverse mode selection for T2VA, FL2VA, and Ref2VA
issues.body:
### Motivation

Dreamverse currently starts every project through one implicit generation path. With FastH3 support now available, users need to declare whether a project is text-only, keyframe-conditioned, or driven by ordered multimodal references before generation begins.

This issue tracks the end-to-end mode-selection experience for the three MiniMax H3 task families:

- **T2VA** — text to video and audio.
- **FL2VA** — first/last-frame to video and audio.
- **Ref2VA** — ordered image, video, and audio references to video and audio.

Use these canonical identifiers in code and protocol payloads: `t2va`, `fl2va`, and `ref2va`.

## Proposed scope

### Frontend

- Add an accessible generation-mode selector to the pre-session Dreamverse composer.
- Default new projects to T2VA.
- Explain the input requirements for each mode.
- Keep the selected mode stable for a project and lock mode changes once its generation session starts.
- Show mode-specific inputs:
  - T2VA: prompt only.
  - FL2VA: first frame and optional last frame, subject to the final product decision.
  - Ref2VA: ordered image/video/audio references.
- Integrate selected assets from the planned Asset List / `@` picker without duplicating asset ownership in the composer.

### Protocol and runtime

- Include `generation_mode` and mode-specific conditioning inputs in project/session initialization.
- Validate mode names and conditioning requirements at the runtime boundary with actionable errors.
- Route T2VA/FL2VA requests to the H3 base pipeline and Ref2VA requests to the H3 reference pipeline/profile.
- Preserve the current WebSocket/session/GPU-pool ownership boundaries.

### Tests

- Cover canonical mode metadata and the T2VA default.
- Cover selection, disabled/busy behavior, and project-init serialization.
- Cover runtime validation for valid modes, unknown modes, and missing/incompatible conditioning inputs.
- Add a mock-server path so the UI flow can be tested without GPUs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A user can choose T2VA, FL2VA, or Ref2VA before starting a project.
- [ ] The UI clearly communicates and collects inputs required by the selected mode.
- [ ] The selected mode and ordered conditioning assets reach the runtime through a typed payload.
- [ ] The runtime rejects invalid combinations and dispatches valid requests to the correct H3 path.
- [ ] Existing LTX/Dreamverse flows remain backward-compatible when `generation_mode` is absent.
- [ ] Frontend, protocol, mock-server, and runtime tests pass.

## Dependencies and coordination

- FastH3 Dreamverse backend foundation: #1800 (merged).
- Asset List is tracked as Aryan's work in the Dreamverse V2 plan; this issue should consume that surface for FL2VA/Ref2VA attachment selection.
- Confirm whether FL2VA accepts first-only and last-only inputs in the product UI, or requires both endpoints.
- Confirm model/profile routing for FastH3 Preview versus base H3 checkpoints before enabling real FL2VA/Ref2VA generation.

### Related resources

- Dreamverse V2 planning document: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Dzty4rIXVNUXZDZH47ia6aw6Ad88RhgBcEMwJ43f2Fs/edit
- FastH3 Dreamverse integration: https://github.com/hao-ai-lab/FastVideo/pull/1800
- MiniMax H3: https://github.com/MiniMax-AI/MiniMax-H3
